overall: The AG found the Fitchburg Historical Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to respond to a minutes request and failing to timely create and approve minutes; it ordered compliance and release of the minutes within 30 days.

allegations.summary: A complainant requested minutes for 2018, 2021 and early 2022 meetings on June 22 and got no response from the Commission.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely respond to a request for meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Found on the AG's own review: the Commission has not timely created and approved minutes, with no staff and drafts still outstanding for past meetings.
allegations.key_passage: we understand, based on the Chair’s communication with our office, that the Commission has failed to timely create and approve meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: The Commission did not respond to the Open Meeting Law complaint within 14 business days, which was not raised in the formal complaint.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
Provide the complainant the requested meeting minutes, whether approved or in draft form, within 30 days of the letter and certify to the AG that it has done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
